newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Swire to ask S&P to consider upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Swire to ask S&P to consider upgrade.

text.p: Swire Pacific Ltd will ask international rating agency Standard and Poor's Corp to consider upgrading the company's credit rating, Peter Johansen, group finance director, said on Thursday.
"We will be talking to S&P in the course of the next few weeks as part of a normal annual review...and we will be putting a case to them to consider upgrading us," Johansen said.
S&P on Wednesday upgraded Hong Kong's long-term foreign currency rating to A-plus/A-1-plus from single-A/A-1.
It also raised Hong Kong's local currency rating to AA-minus/A-1-plus from A-plus/A-1.
The rating agency raised the ratings of a number of Hong Kong companies in conjunction with Hong Kong's upgrade.
It raised the foreign currency ratings of China Light and Power, Hutchsion Whampoa, Sun Hung Kai Properties and the Mass Transit Railway Corp to A-plus from single-A.
On May 6, S&P affirmed Swire Pacific's single-A rating and said that the company's rating outlook was stable.

Speaking on Reuters Financial Television on Thursday, S&P managing director Paul Coughlin pointed out that the companies that were upgraded had both local currency and foreign currency ratings equal to those of Hong Kong.

"The ones that did have their foreign currency ratings upgraded had for some time had the local currency rating of A-plus. So with the foreign currency rating of Hong Kong going up, automatically the foreign currency ratings of those companies would go up," he said.
Coughlin said that while the credit differences between Swire Pacific and the upgraded companies are "minor" there are key issues that constrain Swire's rating.
While Swire is a conservatively managed company and has very solid profitability, its two core businesess, property and airlines, tend to be volatile, he said.
"Around the world both (property and airlines) have a record of volatility so we factored that into the ratings," he said.

Of the companies that were upgraded, "some have even stronger fundamentals than Swire or else, as with Hutchison, they are more diversified and some of their businesses are less volatile," said Coughlin.
